newsitem.title: BULGARIA: World Bank approves $40 million Bulgaria loan.
newsitem.headline: World Bank approves $40 million Bulgaria loan.

text.p: The World Bank has approved a $40 million loan to Bulgaria for imports of essential goods like grain, fuel and medical supplies, a World Bank official said on Friday.
"The board has approved the disbursement of a $40 million loan for critical imports," said an official at the World Bank Sofia office.
The loan is part of a $290 million funding package earmarked for Bulgaria if the government speeds up privatisation of state factories and banks and eliminates public sector losses.
The World Bank and the interim cabinet have agreed on a reform and funding programme consisting of three loans linked to agreements to be reached with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in March.
The IMF approved last month a $657 million funding package.

The second World Bank loan is a social safety net loan of $80 million to be targeted to the most vulnerable social groups like pensioners, jobless and the disabled. The loan will be offered to the board for approval in June.
The third credit, for financial reform and restructuring enterprises, consists of two loans totalling around $170 million.
Liberalisation of prices to increase farm supplies from local producers to offset shortages is also part of the reform targets.

The caretaker cabinet appointed some three months ago has made the first steps to speeding up sell-offs and freeing prices and trade rules. It is due to hand over this month to the new government elected on April 19. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
